note: Social-media 'digital memory' timeline (born at Startup Weekend Copenhagen); 'raised a $2 million funding round led by August Capital and Atomico' (TechCrunch, Sep 2010; the firm's 2011 fund-II page: 'Atomico co-invested in this deal with August Capital') - the round is unnamed; service and accounts deleted 2013-02-22 with the team joining an unnamed company -> defunct (the acqui-hire rule)

Online interior-design marketplace (Brent Hoberman); Atomico is named in the launch investor list beside lead SPARK Ventures (TechCrunch, Feb 2008), the 2007 round that Growth Business calls 'seed' and Global Venturing 'series A' - the name conflicts -> undetermined; the site wound down and redirected to Made.com before Monoqi bought its old assets in Jan 2015 (TechCrunch) -> defunct

Dockless bike sharing (Beijing); the $450M Series D of Mar 2017 led by DST: 'other investors include Didi Chuxing, CITIC Private Equity Funds, Matrix Partners China, Coatue, Atomico and Macrolink Group' (ChinaTravelNews; the firm's own post 'Our investment in ofo'); debt crisis from Dec 2018, no longer operating bike rentals by 2020 (Wikipedia) -> defunct

Hotel booking (Serge Faguet, Kirill Makharinsky); the $13.6M Series A of Jul 2011 'led by General Catalyst Partners and Accel Partners' lists 'Niklas Zennstrom and Atomico (Skype)' among the investors (the company's release; Wikipedia: 'Niklas Zennstrom and Atomico Ventures'); operating, owned by Emerging Travel Group (Interfax, 2026)

Social network for gamers; 'The round was led by Atomico Ventures' - the $2.1M (GBP 1.3M) Series A of Nov 2009 (TechCrunch; Ljungman director 2009-2012, register); the 2008 seed was angels only; acquired by Green Man Gaming 2012-07-09 (Wikipedia)

Ratings-and-reviews software for retailers (founded 2005); on the firm's 2008-2012 listings, but no press names Atomico in any round (2005 A: Menlo, Draper Richards; 2007 $15M: Lehman, Menlo; 2010-2011 rounds) - an unannounced or secondary position, undated -> undetermined; acquired by Bazaarvoice 2012 (TechCrunch), later sold on (Viewpoints 2014, 1WorldSync 2023)

Restaurant reservations for Latin America; 'Atomico Leads Investment Round for Restorando.com' (LAVCA, Apr 2011: $500K with Kaszek) - the entry, unnamed, before the $3.2M Series A of Feb 2012 led by Emergence (the firm's own release) -> undetermined (the ankar reading); acquired by TheFork (TripAdvisor) 2019 (LatAm List)

Video conversations, then social-media clients (Loic Le Meur); the '$6 million Series A round of funding' of Feb 2008 led by Atomico (TechCrunch; Wikipedia: 'the primary one being Atomico'); acquired by HootSuite Sep 2012

Icon-based predictive keyboard (Ed Maklouf, London/Barcelona); 'has raised GBP 550,000 (roughly $880,000) in seed funding from Atomico Ventures' (TechCrunch, Feb 2011); no later round found; Siine Ltd dissolved 2018-12-11 (register) -> defunct; graduation decided in the S2A pass

Structured-data publishing (silk.co, Amsterdam); 'Silk announced it has completed a EUR 320,000 ($475,000) funding round led by Atomico' (TNW; TechCrunch: 'Silk Scores Seed Funding From Atomico'); the next round, NEA's $1.6M of Aug 2012, is also named a seed and no Series A followed; Palantir's 2016 deal was an acqui-hire with silk.co frozen -> defunct (the acqui-hire rule); graduation decided in the S2A pass

Blog search, later a publisher ad platform (Dave Sifry); on the firm's 2008-2012 listings, but no press names Atomico in any round (2006 C: DFJ, Mobius; 2008 D; 2009 extension) - an unannounced or secondary position -> undetermined; acquired by Synacor Feb 2016 for $3M (SiliconANGLE)

Transactional advertising / alternative payments; 'TrialPay raised $12.7m in its February 2008 series B round, receiving funding from VC firms Index Ventures, Atomico and Battery Ventures' (Global Venturing); the 2007 A was Battery and angels; acquired by Visa Feb 2015

Video speed-dating / live video chat (Woo Media, Stephen Stokols); 'We got funded by Niklas Zennstrom and Atomico, his investment vehicle' (socaltech, Nov 2007) - about $5M before Jun 2008 with Mangrove, unnamed and undated; Index led the $12M second round Jun 2008 (CBS); acquired by Zoosk Nov 2011 (Wikipedia)

Social gifting, later card-linked rewards; '$5.5 million in Series A funding ... led by Atomico' (TechCrunch, Nov 2011; Zennstrom to the board; Creandum's seed came earlier); the firm's 2013 release 'Wrapp raises $15m Series B'; acquired by Meniga Jan 2019 (Finovate), as Creandum and Greylock record

Listed on the firm's 2008-2011 sites (rendered 'wunderLOOP'; its own page /OurPortfolio/wunderLOOP.xml is in the CDX but the Internet Archive refused this machine before it could be read); no press, Wikipedia or register record identifies the company -> undetermined in every outcome column, excluded from every metric

Social/casual games group (Zattikka Ltd 2007; Zattikka PLC on AIM 2012, per the firm's own 2012 page); the register dates the position: Zattikka Ltd's annual return to 2009-09-26 lists Atomico Management Limited with 5,333 C ORDINARY shares (transferred 2010-06-24) - no round word; administration Aug 2013 (Game Developer), the PLC dissolved 2019 -> defunct
